rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` has the front matter the `skills` site query recognizes, so it is a site. The requirement lets a skill link to files for specialized material. It requires each such link to say when to read the file.

The file has no Markdown links. It points to other files only through code-span paths, and each of those says when to read the file:
- `references/review-prompt.md`: workflow step 3 (Review) tells the reviewer subagent to read it. If subagents can't be started, the agent reviews each group against it. The step 3 context therefore says when to read it.
- `references/fixme.md`: this belongs to the habeas-evidence skill. The "Choosing references" section cites it for the case "To defer a requirement gap the user agrees to", which says when to read it.

Whether code-span paths count as links is ambiguous. The result is the same on either reading. If they aren't links, the obligation has nothing to govern. If they are, each one states its trigger. Other mentions, such as the habeas skill's `SKILL.md` and sections of habeas-evidence, are references to other skills, not links to this skill's specialized files. I found no gap.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
